questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the native language was english, and that the university had subjects that matched my interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Ofc there is always a lot of new information everytime you attend something new, which can feel overwhelming. But overall it was easy to find the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there were a lack of signing on campus at arrival for us international students, who arrived earlier than the domestic students. But the moment you found your residence there were plenty of assistence. We immidiatly felt like we were in good hands.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: with or without kitchen. Flats with 8 people or small houses hosting 4-5 people.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At my flat we had a kitchen. It was possible to do a full mealplan and a flexible one, for us with a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
they can borrow cuttlery, pans etc. at the residence. 
For european students it is worth noticing, that the rules for on campus living are very strict. No drinking in your flat, at times there is a no guest policy etc, it´s prohibited to enter the balcony etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The residence were a bit old...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You placed your self at the desk at the residence, and then the person working there took care of the rest. Suuuuper easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All kinds of help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: succesful, it is an easy system. I did wish tho, that I new, you could apply for multiple classes and then unsubscribe to the classes you don´t like, later on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registration for classes: subscribe to all the classes you find interesting. Try them out for a week, and then unsubscribe to the once you find least interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of grad courses were generally not higher than undergrad courses. I did notice though, that the level of courses with an european professor were significantly higher than those with a canadian professor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I prefer the style of teaching at UCPH. At my host insitution there were very few lectures, but then a bunch of assignments. Also found it strange that, you are graded for all your work, meaning you can have passed your course even before you take the final exam. 
They also focus a lot on remembering instead of understanding, which I personally find strange.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
quantitative genetics and animal models (grad)
communication and development (grad)
Genetics of companion animals (undergrad)
Epigenetics (undergrad)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: epigenetics were a very interesting course with a very passionate professor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: great atletic centre

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds of clubs and sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: make a dodge-ball team!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: algonguin park were beautiful. If you have the money and time, go visit Banff aswell on the west coast. It is the most amazing place ever!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open, join everything you can. Go to brass taps every tuesday, they have trivial, which is great fun!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: non really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are veery polite and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remeber to have fun! 
travel in the begining of the semester, where school stuff is not as busy.
Visit crellman for lunch or dinner, they have the best food on campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
you can look up a map to find your class online on this webside:
https://classfind.com/guelph

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The enormous and great community we created (we being the international students).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: work-life-balance

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
